children: Thailand's customs-cleared exports (THCEX=ECI) rose 24.0% in September from a year earlier, the commerce ministry said on Monday, higher than analysts expected.

Exports rose for the 27th consecutive month, the ministry said, led by electronics, which was supported by global demand for artificial intelligence products, as well as a rise in agricultural commodity and food shipments
The September reading compared with a forecast rise of 17.85% in a Reuters poll and followed an increase of 24.3% in the previous month
In the January-September period, exports rose 19.6% year on year
Exports may rise 19% this year, the ministry said, up from 15% forecast last month
Exports next year were expected to rise 2% to 4%, Nantapong Chiralerspong, the head of the Commerce Ministry's Trade Policy and Strategy Office, told a news briefing
September exports to the United States, Thailand's largest market, rose 50.1% from a year earlier, while shipments to China increased 18.4%, the ministry said
Imports (THCIM=ECI) rose by a record 50.4% in September compared with a year earlier, higher than the forecast rise of 31.25% in the poll
Thailand recorded a trade deficit (THCTR=ECI) of $5.86 billion in September, compared with a forecast deficit of $1.83 billion
